title: Fix ProfileEditor ISF validation: mg/dL range hardcoded blocks mmol/L users from saving profiles
description: ProfileEditor Zod schema enforces ISF in 10–200 mg/dL/U range with mg/dL error messages for all users, making it impossible for mmol/L users (valid range ~0.5–11.1 mmol/L/U) to save a profile. This is a P0 clinical safety issue: mmol/L patients (e.g. mike) cannot create or edit insulin profiles.
design:
# OpenSpec: Fix ProfileEditor ISF validation to support mmol/L unit (kdiab-spa)

## Goal
ProfileEditor.tsx uses a hardcoded Zod schema (isfSegmentSchema) that enforces ISF values between 10.0 and 200.0 mg/dL/U. mmol/L users (e.g. mike, whose ISF is 0.5-11.1 mmol/L/U) cannot save profiles because the schema rejects their values. glucoseUnit is in App.tsx state but is never passed to ProfileEditor.

## Context
- kdiab-ui/src/features/profiles/ProfileEditor.tsx lines 49-52: isfSegmentSchema hardcoded min 10.0 max 200.0 with mg/dL error messages.
- ProfileEditorProps (lines 114-120): no glucoseUnit field.
- kdiab-ui/src/App.tsx line 39: const [glucoseUnit, setGlucoseUnit] = useState('mg/dL').
- App.tsx lines 258-264: <ProfileEditor userId=... initialProfile=... onProfileSaved=... readOnly=... isDoctor=...> - glucoseUnit not passed.
- profileSchema (lines 62-110) references isfSegmentSchema at module level; both must become dynamic.

## Interface Changes
No API changes - frontend validation only.

## Implementation Plan
1. kdiab-ui/src/features/profiles/ProfileEditor.tsx
   - Remove module-level isfSegmentSchema and profileSchema definitions.
   - Add glucoseUnit?: string to ProfileEditorProps.
   - Inside ProfileEditor function, derive both schemas using useMemo:
     const isfSegmentSchema = useMemo(() =>
       z.object({
         startTime: z.string().regex(/^([0-1]?[0-9]|2[0-3]):[0-5][0-9]$/, 'Invalid time (HH:MM)'),
         value: (glucoseUnit ?? 'mg/dL') === 'mmol/L'
           ? z.number().min(0.5, 'ISF must be >= 0.5 mmol/L/U').max(11.1, 'ISF must be <= 11.1 mmol/L/U')
           : z.number().min(10.0, 'ISF must be >= 10.0 mg/dL/U').max(200.0, 'ISF must be <= 200.0 mg/dL/U'),
       }),
       [glucoseUnit]
     )
   - Move the full profileSchema (with its .refine for total daily basal) inside the component using useMemo([isfSegmentSchema]).
   - Update useForm to use the memoized resolver: resolver: zodResolver(profileSchema).
   - Re-declare type ProfileFormValues = z.infer<typeof profileSchema> inside the component.
2. kdiab-ui/src/App.tsx
   - Pass glucoseUnit={glucoseUnit} to the <ProfileEditor> at lines 258-264.

## Test Plan
- [ ] npm run build in kdiab-ui/ - TypeScript compiles clean
- [ ] npm run lint - no lint errors
- [ ] Manual: mike (mmol/L) adds ISF 2.5 -> save succeeds
- [ ] Manual: sarah (mg/dL) adds ISF 150 -> save succeeds
- [ ] Manual: mike adds ISF 12.0 -> error shown
- [ ] Manual: sarah adds ISF 201 -> error shown

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] mmol/L users can save ISF values in range 0.5-11.1 mmol/L/U
- [ ] mg/dL users retain 10-200 mg/dL/U constraint
- [ ] Error messages include correct unit label
- [ ] TypeScript compiles clean; lint passes

## Risks & Assumptions
- ISF conversion: 10 mg/dL/U / 18 = 0.56, 200 / 18 = 11.1 - safe to round to 0.5 and 11.1.
- useForm zodResolver is recreated when profileSchema changes (memoized).
- type ProfileFormValues must remain consistent; move type alias inside component.

title: Fix AnalyticsService: pass from/to date range to measuresClient in getAgp and getHba1c
description: AnalyticsService.getAgp() and getHba1c() call measuresClient.getMeasures() without from/to parameters, fetching ALL user measures (up to 50K records) and filtering in-memory. Now that kdiab-wrt added from/to support to the measures endpoint, AnalyticsService should pass the caller's date range to measuresClient so only the relevant window of CGM data is fetched. Without this fix, every analytics request is a full table scan regardless of the selected time range.

# OpenSpec: Pass from/to to getMeasures in AnalyticsService (kdiab-2zu)

## Goal
AnalyticsService.getAgp() and fetchCgmReadings() (used by getHba1c()) call measuresClient.getMeasures() without from/to parameters, causing a full upstream fetch of all measures. MeasuresClient.getMeasures() already accepts from: String? and to: String? (implemented by kdiab-wrt). Simply pass them through to eliminate the full table scan and redundant client-side date filter.

## Context
- kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/.../application/service/AnalyticsService.kt:
  - Line 69 (in getAgp()): measuresClient.getMeasures(userId, authorization, correlationId) - no from/to.
  - Line 115 (in fetchCgmReadings()): same.
  - Lines 74-76 (in getAgp()): if (t < fromInstant || t > toInstant) return@forEach - redundant post-fetch filter.
  - Lines 116-120 (in fetchCgmReadings()): .filter { t >= fromInstant && t <= toInstant } - redundant.
- MeasuresClient.getMeasures() signature: (userId, authorization, correlationId, from: String? = null, to: String? = null). Client appends ?from=...&to=... when non-null.
- TimelineService already passes from/to correctly (line 27).

## Interface Changes
No interface changes - internal call-site fix only.

## Implementation Plan
1. kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/.../application/service/AnalyticsService.kt
   - In getAgp() line 69: change to measuresClient.getMeasures(userId, authorization, correlationId, from, to).
   - Remove the 'if (t < fromInstant || t > toInstant) return@forEach' guard in getAgp() (lines 74-76). Keep Instant.parse and UTC hour extraction.
   - In fetchCgmReadings() line 115: change to measuresClient.getMeasures(userId, authorization, correlationId, from, to).
   - Remove the .filter { t >= fromInstant && t <= toInstant } block (lines 116-120). Remove fromInstant/toInstant variables from fetchCgmReadings (no longer needed there).

## Test Plan
- [ ] ./gradlew :backend:check --no-daemon from kdiab-analyze/ - all existing tests pass, Detekt clean, Kover >= 80%
- [ ] Manual: open HbA1c for sarah with 7-day window - check backend logs show ?from=...&to=... in upstream URL

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Both getMeasures() calls pass from and to to MeasuresClient
- [ ] Redundant client-side date filters removed
- [ ] ./gradlew :backend:check passes

## Risks & Assumptions
- kdiab-measures endpoint already handles from/to (kdiab-wrt). No measures service change needed.
- fromInstant/toInstant are still needed in getAgp() for UTC hour grouping - do NOT remove those Instant.parse calls from getAgp, only the range-filter guard (lines 74-76).

title: Consolidate all four frontends into a single kdiab-ui application
description:
The platform currently has four separate React frontends (kdiab-measures/frontend, kdiab-profiles/frontend, kdiab-treatments/frontend, kdiab-analyze/frontend). Each has its own Vite build, its own Keycloak client, its own nginx container, and its own OIDC login flow. This creates UX fragmentation (separate logins per service pre-SSO fix), maintenance overhead (four identical build pipelines, four sets of dependencies, duplicated i18n/theme/auth boilerplate), and blocks features like cross-service navigation.

Goal: create a single `kdiab-ui/` module at the monorepo root that combines all four feature areas into one React SPA. Each backend service is unchanged — only the frontend layer is consolidated.

## What moves into kdiab-ui

All feature code from the four existing frontends:

| Source | Feature directory | Destination |
|---|---|---|
| kdiab-measures/frontend | src/features/measures/ | kdiab-ui/src/features/measures/ |
| kdiab-profiles/frontend | src/features/profiles/ | kdiab-ui/src/features/profiles/ |
| kdiab-treatments/frontend | src/features/treatments/ | kdiab-ui/src/features/treatments/ |
| kdiab-analyze/frontend | src/features/timeline/ | kdiab-ui/src/features/timeline/ |
| kdiab-analyze/frontend | src/features/analytics/ | kdiab-ui/src/features/analytics/ |
| kdiab-analyze/frontend | src/features/timeframe/ | kdiab-ui/src/features/timeframe/ |

Shared infrastructure (pick once, deduplicate):
- Single `src/api/` with generated clients for all four OpenAPI specs (measures, profiles, treatments, analyze)
- Single `src/auth/` (react-oidc-context, one Keycloak client: `kdiab-ui`)
- Single `src/i18n/` (merge all locale files from all four frontends)
- Single `src/styles/` (CSS custom properties, one dark theme)
- Single `App.tsx` with top-level navigation (tab bar or sidebar: Measures | Profiles | Treatments | Analytics)

## New Keycloak client

Add a `kdiab-ui` client to `config/keycloak-realm.json` with:
- All four audience mappers (measure, profile, treatment, analyze) — same as kdiab-analyze-frontend today
- All existing protocol mappers (roles, allowed_patients, glucose_unit, weight_unit)
- PKCE S256

The four existing Keycloak clients (kdiab-measures-frontend, kdiab-profiles-frontend, kdiab-treatments-frontend, kdiab-analyze-frontend) can be kept for backwards compatibility or removed.

## Vite / build setup

- Single `package.json`, single `vite.config.ts`
- API generation script runs all four `openapi-generator-cli generate` commands (one per service spec)
- Single `Dockerfile` producing one nginx container (port 3000), replacing the four individual frontend Dockerfiles
- `VITE_BASE_PATH=/` — no sub-path prefix needed since there is only one frontend
- Single nginx.conf: serve static assets at `/`; proxy each service's API at its path prefix (`/api/measures/`, `/api/profiles/`, `/api/treatments/`, `/api/analyze/`)

## API routing in kdiab-ui nginx

Each backend API remains at its own port. The unified nginx proxies by prefix:

```nginx
location /api/measures/  { proxy_pass http://measures-backend:8080/api/; }
location /api/profiles/  { proxy_pass http://profiles-backend:8082/api/; }
location /api/treatments/ { proxy_pass http://treatments-backend:8083/api/; }
location /api/analyze/   { proxy_pass http://analyze-backend:8084/api/; }
location /               { root /usr/share/nginx/html; try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html; }
```

The generated API clients set their basePath to `/api/measures/`, `/api/profiles/`, etc.

## docker-compose.yml changes

- Remove: measures-frontend, profiles-frontend, treatments-frontend, analyze-frontend containers
- Add: kdiab-ui container (builds from kdiab-ui/, serves on port 3000)
- Gateway simplifies to just kdiab-ui (or can be removed entirely if kdiab-ui IS the gateway)

## What to delete after migration

- kdiab-measures/frontend/
- kdiab-profiles/frontend/
- kdiab-treatments/frontend/
- kdiab-analyze/frontend/
- The four per-service frontend nginx.conf files
- The four frontend Dockerfiles

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `cd kdiab-ui && npm run build` succeeds with no TypeScript errors
- [ ] `docker compose up --build` starts the platform with a single frontend container at localhost:3000
- [ ] All four feature areas (Measures, Profiles, Treatments, Analytics) are reachable from the unified navigation
- [ ] Logging in once grants access to all features — no per-service login screen
- [ ] Role-based UI elements (doctor vs patient vs admin views) work correctly
- [ ] mmol/L and mg/dL unit preferences apply across all glucose-displaying features
- [ ] `npm run lint` and `npm run build` pass with zero errors

design:
# OpenSpec: fix BFF analytics sgv→value field name (kdiab-ko5)

## Goal
Fix the BFF AnalyticsService so that HbA1c, TIR, and AGP compute correctly. The root cause is that AnalyticsService reads data["sgv"] (Nightscout convention) but all measure data now uses data["value"] (kdiab canonical schema). Two callsites in production code and three test helper methods use the wrong field name.

## Context

### Root cause
When seed data was normalised from Nightscout conventions (sgv/mbg fields) to the canonical kdiab schema (value/unit/trend), only the frontend MeasureList.tsx was updated. The BFF AnalyticsService still reads the Nightscout field name, causing every CGM lookup to return null and all analytics to silently compute with zero readings.

### Files that need changing

**Production code:**
- kdiab-bff/backend/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/bff/application/service/AnalyticsService.kt
  - Line 68  (getAgp):           data["sgv"]  → data["value"]
  - Line 111 (fetchCgmReadings): data["sgv"]  → data["value"]

**Test helpers:**
- kdiab-bff/backend/src/test/kotlin/.../service/AnalyticsServiceTest.kt
  - Line 30: put("sgv", sgv)   → put("value", sgv); add put("unit", "mg/dL")
- kdiab-bff/backend/src/test/kotlin/.../service/TimelineServiceTest.kt
  - Line 29: put("sgv", 120.0) → put("value", 120.0); add put("unit", "mg/dL")
- kdiab-bff/backend/src/test/kotlin/.../http/MeasuresClientTest.kt
  - Line 31: put("sgv", sgv)   → put("value", sgv); add put("unit", "mg/dL")

## Interface Changes
No interface changes — the fix is internal to AnalyticsService and test helpers.

## Implementation Plan
1. AnalyticsService.kt line 68:  data["sgv"] → data["value"]
2. AnalyticsService.kt line 111: data["sgv"] → data["value"]
3. AnalyticsServiceTest.kt line 30: put("sgv", sgv) → put("value", sgv) and add put("unit", "mg/dL")
4. TimelineServiceTest.kt line 29: put("sgv", 120.0) → put("value", 120.0) and add put("unit", "mg/dL")
5. MeasuresClientTest.kt line 31: put("sgv", sgv) → put("value", sgv) and add put("unit", "mg/dL")
6. Run ./gradlew :backend:check in kdiab-bff — all existing analytics tests must pass

## Test Plan
- [ ] Unit: existing AnalyticsServiceTest cases now receive non-null cgm values and produce non-zero HbA1c/TIR/AGP results
- [ ] Quality gate: cd kdiab-bff && ./gradlew :backend:check passes (Detekt green, Kover ≥ 80%)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] HbA1c endpoint returns a non-null hba1c value when CGM readings exist in the timeframe
- [ ] TIR breakdown returns non-zero inRangeCount/belowCount/aboveCount when CGM readings exist
- [ ] AGP hourly buckets contain non-zero count values for hours with CGM readings
- [ ] ./gradlew :backend:check passes with no regressions

## Risks & Assumptions
- The fix is a pure rename — no logic changes, no risk of regressions beyond what tests cover.
- The mmol/L conversion (glucoseUnit JWT claim × 18) may also be wrong now that ALL values are stored in mg/dL regardless of user preference. This is a separate P1 issue and is out of scope for this fix.

title: Fix BGM field name mismatch: AddMeasureModal saves value but MeasureList reads mbg
description: AddMeasureModal.tsx saves a BGM reading as {value: 120, unit: 'mg/dL'} but MeasureList.tsx renderDataSummary() reads d.mbg (Nightscout field name). When the field is missing it falls back to JSON.stringify(d), showing raw JSON instead of the formatted glucose value. This means every user-created BGM reading displays incorrectly. Fix: align field name in the modal to use 'mbg' per Nightscout convention, or make the list reader check both 'mbg' and 'value' as fallback.
close_reason: Implemented per approved plan. Tests green, builds clean.

title: Fix silent API failure in AddMeasureModal and AddTreatmentModal
description: When a treatment or measure API call fails (network error, 5xx, 401), the modal closes or stays open with no feedback. The user believes the entry was saved. This is a safety risk: a logged bolus that silently failed means the patient's record is missing a critical event and the doctor cannot see it. Fix: show inline error message in the modal with the failure reason and a retry button. On 401, show 'Session expired - please log in again'.
close_reason: Implemented per approved plan. Tests green, builds clean.

title: Enforce Kover coverage gate in kdiab-analyze: verify task configured but not set to fail build
description: kdiab-analyze/build.gradle.kts has a Kover verify rule defined but the fail-on-violation setting is not enforced — the build succeeds even when coverage drops below the threshold. Unlike the other three services which have properly enforced 80% gates, kdiab-analyze's gate is effectively toothless.

title: Fix missing error states in AnalyticsView and ProfilesView: API failures show blank instead of error message
description: AnalyticsView does not handle query errors from HbA1c or AGP API calls; users see a silent blank where data should appear. ProfilesView similarly shows only loading/success states. Both components need an error state that tells the clinician the data could not be loaded.

title: Fix BFF domain models: use kotlin.uuid.Uuid and kotlinx.datetime.Instant instead of String
description: Timeline, TimelineMeasure, and TimelineTreatment domain models in kdiab-analyze use raw String for all identifiers (userId, id) and timestamps (measuredAt, treatedAt), losing type safety compared to upstream services that use kotlin.uuid.Uuid and kotlinx.datetime.Instant. Parse errors on malformed IDs silently produce wrong results.

title: Add HTTP timeouts to TreatmentsClient and ProfilesClient (only MeasuresClient has them)
description: MeasuresClient has connect/request/socket timeout configuration but TreatmentsClient and ProfilesClient have no explicit timeout setup. A slow treatments or profiles upstream will block the BFF coroutine indefinitely, creating asymmetric failure modes and eventual thread pool exhaustion.

title: Fix unsafe TypeScript type assertions in kdiab-ui: AgpChart non-null percentiles, Error casts, TimeFormatContext useState
description: Three distinct unsafe patterns: (1) AgpChart uses d.p10!, d.p25!, d.p75!, d.p90! non-null assertions on nullable percentile fields after filtering only for d.median !== null; (2) ProfileList and AdminInsulinManager cast error as Error without type guards; (3) TimeFormatContext passes getInitialLocale function reference to useState instead of calling it (getInitialLocale()), causing stale initial state.

title: Validate JWT audience at BFF layer before forwarding tokens to upstream services
description: BffRoutes.kt forwards the Authorization header to upstream services without verifying the JWT audience includes the target service (measure/treatment/profile). A token issued only for the 'analyze' audience would be accepted by the BFF but rejected by upstreams with a 401, producing confusing cascading errors rather than a clear 403 at the BFF.

title: Add circuit breaker to BFF upstream HTTP calls
description: kdiab-analyze has no circuit breaker (e.g. Resilience4j). When an upstream service (measures/treatments/profiles) is degraded, every BFF request waits for the full timeout before failing, exhausting the Ktor thread pool. A circuit breaker that opens after N failures would fail fast and protect the BFF.

title: Fix TypeScript: TimelineResponse interface missing errors array field from kdiab-4c7 implementation
description: kdiab-4c7 added an errors: List<String> field to TimelineService and its Kotlin response type, but the TypeScript analyzeApi.ts TimelineResponse interface was never updated to include errors. The frontend cannot display partial upstream failure information to clinicians.

title: Fix CONTRIBUTING.md: references removed build.sh, non-existent service frontend dirs, and wrong Gradle syntax
description: CONTRIBUTING.md quality gate section references ./build.sh --check (removed in the Gradle migration), cd frontend && npm run dev (frontends consolidated into kdiab-ui), and :backend:check task syntax (does not exist at service level). Contributor onboarding is broken.

title: Fix /readyz probe: verify upstream service availability before reporting ready
description: The /readyz endpoint in kdiab-analyze returns 200 OK without checking whether upstream services (measures, treatments, profiles) are reachable. A freshly started analyze container incorrectly signals ready while its dependencies are still starting, causing load balancers to route traffic before the BFF can actually serve requests.

title: Add retry logic to BFF HTTP clients for transient upstream failures
description: MeasuresClient, TreatmentsClient, and ProfilesClient have no retry policy — a single transient timeout or 5xx response immediately causes 502 Bad Gateway. Adding exponential backoff with 2-3 retries for idempotent GET requests would significantly improve resilience against brief upstream hiccups.

title: Fix documentation port mismatches: gateway documented as 3000 (actual 3005), analyze OpenAPI as 8083 (actual 8084)
description: README.md and CLAUDE.md document the gateway at localhost:3000 but docker-compose.yml maps kdiab-ui to port 3005. kdiab-analyze/api/openapi.yaml server URL lists port 8083 but the service runs on 8084. architecture.adoc still lists old per-service frontend ports (3000–3003) that no longer exist.

design:
# OpenSpec: Add DateTimeParseException and ExposedSQLException handlers to StatusPages (kdiab-705)

## Goal
kdiab-measures, kdiab-treatments, and kdiab-analyze StatusPages plugins do not handle DateTimeParseException/DateTimeFormatException or ExposedSQLException. An invalid from/to query param causes a 500 instead of 400. A DB unique constraint violation returns 500 instead of 409. kdiab-profiles/plugins/StatusPages.kt is the reference implementation.

## Context

title: Gateway root redirect sends browser to localhost:8080/measures instead of localhost:3000/measures
SSO across all kdiab frontends: silent re-auth via shared Keycloak session
description:
When a user is already logged into one kdiab frontend (e.g. kdiab-measures) and navigates to another (e.g. kdiab-analyze), they are prompted to log in again. The existing Keycloak session should be reused silently — the user should land directly in the new service without a login screen.

## Background

All four frontends are OIDC public clients in the same Keycloak realm (`kdiab`). Keycloak maintains a realm-level SSO session cookie (`KEYCLOAK_SESSION`) in the browser after the first login. Any subsequent authorization request from a different client in the same realm can use `prompt=none` to silently exchange the session cookie for a new token without user interaction.

`react-oidc-context` (used by all four frontends) wraps `oidc-client-ts`, which supports silent renew and silent sign-in via a hidden iframe or redirect. The library exposes `signinSilent()` for this purpose.

## Goal

Each frontend should attempt a silent sign-in on startup before showing a login button. If the user already has an active Keycloak session from any other kdiab client, they are authenticated immediately. Only if silent sign-in fails (no existing session, expired session) should the explicit login screen be shown.

## Implementation hints

`react-oidc-context` `AuthProvider` accepts an `onSigninCallback` and supports automatic silent sign-in. The key config additions per frontend:

```tsx
<AuthProvider
  ...
  automaticSilentRenew={true}
  silentRequestTimeoutInSeconds={5}
>
```

On startup, after `useAuth` returns `!auth.isAuthenticated && !auth.isLoading`, call `auth.signinSilent()` before falling back to `auth.signinRedirect()`. This requires a `silent_redirect_uri` pointing to a minimal HTML page that calls `oidc-client-ts`' `signinSilentCallback()`.

Each frontend needs:
1. `public/silent-renew.html` — silent callback page (standard oidc-client-ts boilerplate)
2. `VITE_OIDC_SILENT_REDIRECT_URI` env var (or hardcoded `/silent-renew.html` relative path)
3. `silentRequestTimeoutInSeconds` added to `AuthProvider`
4. Startup logic: try `signinSilent()` first, redirect to login only on failure

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Logging into kdiab-measures and then opening kdiab-profiles in the same browser tab (or a new tab) does not show the Keycloak login page — the user lands authenticated.
- [ ] First visit with no existing session still shows the normal login flow.
- [ ] Session expiry triggers silent renewal without interrupting the user.
- [ ] All four frontends implement the silent sign-in pattern consistently.

# OpenSpec: Partial upstream failure in TimelineService with supervisorScope (kdiab-4c7)

## Goal
TimelineService.getTimeline() uses coroutineScope { async {} } for parallel upstream calls. If either the measures or treatments service fails with UpstreamException, the whole timeline request returns 502. Switch to supervisorScope so a single upstream failure returns the available data plus an errors list indicating which service(s) failed.

## Context

Current state:
- kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/analyze/application/service/TimelineService.kt line 22: = coroutineScope { — a single child failure cancels all siblings.
- kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/analyze/domain/model/Timeline.kt — Timeline(measures, treatments), no errors field.
- kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/analyze/adapters/inbound/web/BffMapper.kt — TimelineResponse has measures and treatments only; Timeline.toResponse() maps both lists.
- kdiab-analyze/api/openapi.yaml — TimelineResponse schema has required: [measures, treatments] with no errors field.
- StatusPages.kt maps UpstreamException to 502. After this fix, timeline will never throw UpstreamException — it always returns 200 with partial data.

## Interface Changes

    TimelineResponse:
      type: object
      required: [measures, treatments]
      properties:
        measures:
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/TimelineMeasure'
        treatments:
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/TimelineTreatment'
        errors:
          type: array
          items:
            type: string
          description: Non-empty when one or more upstream services were unavailable.

## Implementation Plan

1. kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/analyze/domain/model/Timeline.kt — Add val errors: List<String> = emptyList() to the Timeline data class.

title: Forward X-Correlation-ID from BFF to all upstream service calls
description: The BFF correctly generates/extracts X-Correlation-ID from inbound requests (Logging.kt CallId plugin) and binds it to MDC. But MeasuresClient, ProfilesClient, and TreatmentsClient do not forward it in outbound HTTP calls. design:
# OpenSpec: Forward X-Correlation-ID from BFF to upstream services (kdiab-nf3)

## Goal
The BFF extracts `X-Correlation-ID` from every inbound request (via Ktor's `CallId` plugin) and
binds it to SLF4J MDC for local logging — but never forwards it to `MeasuresClient`,
`ProfilesClient`, or `TreatmentsClient`. Distributed tracing is broken: a single user request
cannot be correlated across BFF + measures + profiles + treatments logs. This spec threads the
correlation ID through every layer using the same pattern already used for the `authorization`
header.

## Context

### How authorization is currently forwarded (pattern to replicate)
- `BffRoutes.kt` extracts `Authorization` header into `RequestContext.authorization: String`
- Route handlers pass `authorization` to service methods
- Service methods pass it to client methods
- Client methods set `header(HttpHeaders.Authorization, authorization)` on every HTTP request

### Correlation ID availability
- `Logging.kt` installs `CallId { header("X-Correlation-ID"); generate { UUID.randomUUID() } }`
- Downstream: `call.callId: String?` — always non-null after `generate {}` is configured
- Null-safety: use `call.callId ?: ""` as a safe default (generate always fires in practice)

### Files that need changing

**Inbound:**
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/bff/adapters/inbound/web/BffRoutes.kt`

**Application services:**
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/bff/application/service/TimelineService.kt`
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/bff/application/service/AnalyticsService.kt`
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/bff/application/service/ProfilesService.kt`

**Outbound HTTP clients:**
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/bff/adapters/outbound/http/MeasuresClient.kt`
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/bff/adapters/outbound/http/ProfilesClient.kt`
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/bff/adapters/outbound/http/TreatmentsClient.kt`

**Tests:**
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/test/kotlin/.../service/TimelineServiceTest.kt`
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/test/kotlin/.../service/AnalyticsServiceTest.kt`
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/test/kotlin/.../http/MeasuresClientTest.kt`
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/test/kotlin/.../http/ProfilesClientTest.kt`
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/test/kotlin/.../http/TreatmentsClientTest.kt`

## Interface Changes
No OpenAPI contract changes — `X-Correlation-ID` is a transparent infrastructure header, not part
of the application API.

Function signatures change (internal only):
- `getMeasures(userId, authorization)` → `getMeasures(userId, authorization, correlationId)`
- `getProfiles(userId, authorization)` → `getProfiles(userId, authorization, correlationId)`
- `getTreatments(userId, authorization)` → `getTreatments(userId, authorization, correlationId)`
- Same threading through all service methods.

## Implementation Plan

**Step 1** — `BffRoutes.kt`: Add `correlationId: String` to `RequestContext`; extract via
`call.callId ?: ""` in `extractContext()`; pass to all six service-method call sites:
`timelineService.getTimeline(...)`, `analyticsService.getHba1c(...)`, `analyticsService.getAgp(...)`,
`profilesService.getProfiles(...)`.

**Step 2** — `TimelineService.kt`: Add `correlationId: String` to `getTimeline(...)` signature;
forward to `measuresClient.getMeasures(...)` and `treatmentsClient.getTreatments(...)`.

**Step 3** — `AnalyticsService.kt`: Add `correlationId: String` to `getHba1c(...)`, `getAgp(...)`,
and the private `fetchCgmReadings(...)` helper; forward to `measuresClient.getMeasures(...)`.

**Step 4** — `ProfilesService.kt`: Add `correlationId: String` to `getProfiles(...)`; forward to
`profilesClient.getProfiles(...)`.

**Step 5** — `MeasuresClient.kt`: Add `correlationId: String` to `getMeasures(...)`; add
`header("X-Correlation-ID", correlationId)` to every `httpClient.get()` call (both the loop
iterations in the paginated implementation).

**Step 6** — `ProfilesClient.kt`: Add `correlationId: String` to `getProfiles(...)`; add
`header("X-Correlation-ID", correlationId)` to the `httpClient.get()` call.

**Step 7** — `TreatmentsClient.kt`: Add `correlationId: String` to `getTreatments(...)`; add
`header("X-Correlation-ID", correlationId)` to the `httpClient.get()` call.

**Step 8** — `MeasuresClientTest.kt`: Add `correlationId = "test-cid"` to all `getMeasures()`
calls; add a test `getMeasures sends X-Correlation-ID header` that captures request headers with
`MockEngine` and asserts `"X-Correlation-ID" == "test-cid"`.

**Step 9** — `ProfilesClientTest.kt`: Same as Step 8 for `getProfiles`.

**Step 10** — `TreatmentsClientTest.kt`: Same as Step 8 for `getTreatments`.

**Step 11** — `AnalyticsServiceTest.kt`: Add `correlationId = ""` to all service-method calls.

**Step 12** — `TimelineServiceTest.kt`: Add `correlationId = ""` to all service-method calls.

(Check for `ProfilesServiceTest.kt` — add `correlationId = ""` if it exists.)

## Test Plan
- [ ] Unit: new header-forwarding test in each of the three client test files verifies that
  `X-Correlation-ID` with the supplied value is sent on every upstream request
- [ ] Unit: existing AnalyticsServiceTest and TimelineServiceTest compile and pass with updated signatures
- [ ] Quality gate: `cd kdiab-bff && ./gradlew :backend:check` — all tests green, Detekt clean, Kover ≥ 80%

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every outbound HTTP call from BFF to kdiab-measures, kdiab-profiles, kdiab-treatments carries
  `X-Correlation-ID` header equal to the value extracted from the inbound request (or a
  generated UUID when the client did not supply one)
- [ ] New unit tests in MeasuresClientTest, ProfilesClientTest, TreatmentsClientTest confirm the
  header is present and correctly valued
- [ ] `./gradlew :backend:check` passes with no regressions

## Risks & Assumptions
- `call.callId` is always non-null after `generate {}` is configured — using `?: ""` as a
  defensive fallback only; in practice the empty string path will never be taken.
- No changes needed to upstream services (measures, profiles, treatments) — they already accept
  `X-Correlation-ID` via their own `Logging.kt` CallId plugin configuration.
- No OpenAPI schema changes, no frontend changes, no DB changes.

title: Add HTTP connect/request/socket timeouts to BFF HttpClient
description: BFF Application.kt instantiates an HttpClient with CIO engine but no timeout configuration. If any upstream service hangs, the BFF request blocks indefinitely, exhausting the Ktor dispatcher thread pool and cascading failure to all concurrent requests. Fix: install HttpTimeout plugin with connectTimeoutMillis=5000, requestTimeoutMillis=10000, socketTimeoutMillis=5000 in the HttpClient block in Application.kt.

title: Add audit logging for doctor access to patient data
description: There is no audit trail when a doctor reads or writes patient data (views timeline, proposes profile, views analytics). This is required for HIPAA/GDPR compliance. Every doctor read/write must log: timestamp, doctorId, patientId, action (viewed-timeline, proposed-profile, viewed-analytics), and IP/user-agent. Store in an immutable audit table. Expose read-only audit log endpoint for admins. Affects all four backend services.

title: Add SerializationException and JsonConvertException handlers to all StatusPages
description: When call.receive<T>() is called on malformed JSON, Ktor throws SerializationException or JsonConvertException. None of the four services' StatusPages plugins catch these. They propagate as unhandled exceptions and return a non-JSON 500 instead of a structured 400 ErrorResponse. Fix: add exception<SerializationException> and exception<JsonConvertException> handlers to all four StatusPages.kt files returning HttpStatusCode.BadRequest with ErrorResponse.

# OpenSpec: Replace eclipse-temurin Docker Hub base images with GHCR equivalents

## Goal
Replace docker.io/library/eclipse-temurin base images in all four backend Dockerfiles with ghcr.io/adoptium/temurin21-jdk and ghcr.io/adoptium/temurin21-jre from GitHub Container Registry, which has no pull rate limits. Also update dependabot.yml so it tracks the new image names.

## Context
All four backend Dockerfiles are structurally identical, using a two-stage build:
- Stage 1 (builder): FROM eclipse-temurin:21-jdk-alpine AS builder — pulls from docker.io, rate-limited
- Stage 2 (runtime): FROM eclipse-temurin:21-jre-alpine — pulls from docker.io, rate-limited

Affected files:
- kdiab-measures/backend/Dockerfile
- kdiab-profiles/backend/Dockerfile
- kdiab-treatments/backend/Dockerfile
- kdiab-bff/backend/Dockerfile
- .github/dependabot.yml — has ignore: eclipse-temurin >= 22 in four docker sections; must be updated to new image names

## Interface Changes
No interface changes. Pure infrastructure change.

## Implementation Plan

### Step 1 — Verify GHCR Alpine tags exist
Before editing, pull-test the candidate images:
  podman pull ghcr.io/adoptium/temurin21-jdk:21-alpine
  podman pull ghcr.io/adoptium/temurin21-jre:21-alpine
If either pull fails, fall back to the Ubuntu-slim tag (:21) for that image.
IMPORTANT: if falling back to Ubuntu image, addgroup -S/adduser -S (BusyBox/Alpine syntax) in the runtime stage must change to groupadd -r/useradd -r -g ktor ktor (GNU/Linux syntax).

### Step 2 — Update all four Dockerfiles
In each Dockerfile make exactly two FROM substitutions:
  FROM eclipse-temurin:21-jdk-alpine AS builder
  → FROM ghcr.io/adoptium/temurin21-jdk:21-alpine AS builder

  FROM eclipse-temurin:21-jre-alpine
  → FROM ghcr.io/adoptium/temurin21-jre:21-alpine

No other lines change (assuming Alpine tags exist and are confirmed in step 1).

### Step 3 — Update .github/dependabot.yml
The four package-ecosystem: docker entries for backend dirs currently ignore eclipse-temurin. Replace each with the two new image names:
  ignore:
    - dependency-name: temurin21-jdk
      versions: ['>= 22']
    - dependency-name: temurin21-jre
      versions: ['>= 22']

### Step 4 — Smoke-build one image
  cd /home/triplem/projects/kdiab
  BUILDAH_FORMAT=docker podman build -f kdiab-bff/backend/Dockerfile kdiab-bff -t test-bff-backend
Confirm exit code 0 and no rate-limit errors. Clean up: podman rmi test-bff-backend.

### Step 5 — Commit and close issue
Commit message: fix(docker): replace eclipse-temurin Docker Hub images with GHCR equivalents
Then: bd close kdiab-78y

## Test Plan
- [ ] podman pull ghcr.io/adoptium/temurin21-jdk:21-alpine succeeds with no rate-limit error
- [ ] podman pull ghcr.io/adoptium/temurin21-jre:21-alpine succeeds
- [ ] podman build of kdiab-bff backend exits 0
- [ ] No unit tests affected — pure Dockerfile/YAML change

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All four backend Dockerfiles reference ghcr.io/adoptium/* images only
- [ ] podman compose up --build succeeds from a clean-cache state
- [ ] dependabot.yml ignore rules reference the new image names
- [ ] No functional change to the running application

## Risks & Assumptions
- ghcr.io/adoptium/temurin21-jdk:21-alpine may not exist → fall back to :21 (Ubuntu-slim); agent must verify with pull-test first
- If Ubuntu fallback needed: Alpine addgroup -S/adduser -S syntax must change to GNU equivalents
- Adoptium GHCR images are the same JDK build as Docker Hub eclipse-temurin (same upstream source)

title: kdiab-bff: Backend-for-Frontend with analytics dashboard
description: New kdiab-bff service aggregating measures, treatments, and profiles into a unified analytics frontend. Features: combined CGM+treatment timeline chart, HbA1c/TIR analytics, AGP (ambulatory glucose profile by hour), profiles viewer. Stack: Kotlin/Ktor backend (stateless, HTTP clients to upstream services), React+Recharts frontend. Ports: backend 8083, frontend 3003.
close_reason: kdiab-bff service fully implemented: backend (services, routes, HTTP clients, domain, plugins, Application.kt, Dockerfile) and frontend (App.tsx, Tab nav, TimelineChart, AgpChart, HbA1cCard, TimeInRangeBar, ProfilesTable, i18n, Recharts)

title: Add distributed tracing infrastructure (OpenTelemetry) to BFF and upstream services
description: The platform forwards X-Correlation-ID between services via HTTP headers and MDC, but no trace spans are collected or exported. Without OpenTelemetry or equivalent, multi-service latency breakdowns are invisible and diagnosing slow requests requires correlating logs manually across four service log streams.

title: Fix ISF and target glucose labels in ProfileList and ProfileEditor: show correct unit based on user preference
description: ProfileList displays ISF and BG Target values with hardcoded 'mg/dL' labels regardless of the user's glucoseUnit setting. ProfileEditor placeholders for ISF and target glucose fields also hardcode 'mg/dL'. mmol/L users see incorrect units throughout the profile management UI.

title: Add zero basal segment safety warning in ProfileEditor
description: ProfileEditor allows basal segments with rate 0.0 U/h (the default for new segments) without any warning. A profile with zero basal and no bolus results in no insulin delivery — a life-threatening configuration for T1D patients. A validation warning should alert the user when any segment has a zero rate.

title: Fix wildcard webOrigins in kdiab-analyze/config/keycloak-realm.json per-service Keycloak config
description: The per-service standalone Keycloak config at kdiab-analyze/config/keycloak-realm.json uses webOrigins: ['*'], allowing any origin to obtain tokens. kdiab-ycr fixed the root config/keycloak-realm.json, but the standalone per-service config was not updated and still has the wildcard.

title: Add MeasuresClientTest scenarios for network timeouts and transient HTTP failures in pagination loop
description: MeasuresClientTest does not cover cases where a page request times out mid-pagination or returns a 5xx error partway through the loop. These failures currently throw UpstreamException mid-fetch, leaving partially collected pages silently discarded. Tests should verify both the error path and the page boundary behaviour.

title: Create ADRs for: BFF architecture, API-first design, kdiab-ui UI consolidation, single-stage Docker builds
description: Four significant architectural decisions lack formal ADR documentation in docs/adr/: (1) kdiab-analyze as stateless BFF aggregator, (2) API-first design with OpenAPI code generation on both sides, (3) consolidation of four per-service frontends into unified kdiab-ui gateway, (4) single-stage Dockerfile copying pre-built JARs. All are described informally in CLAUDE.md but never recorded as decision records.

title: Add security audit trail for authentication events: login failures, token rejections, and 403s
description: kdiab-profiles and kdiab-measures only audit doctor access to patient data. Failed JWT validation, 401 responses, and 403 authorization denials are only written to SLF4J logs (not the audit table), making security incident investigation difficult. Auth events should be recorded with timestamp, userId (if extractable), and endpoint.

title: Add MEAL and ACTIVITY treatment types to TimelineChart color map
description: TimelineChart.tsx TREATMENT_COLORS map (or TREATMENT_CATEGORY map from kdiab-rua) does not include MEAL or ACTIVITY types, so those treatment scatter points render as the default gray fallback color. MEAL and ACTIVITY are significant daily T1D events that should be visually distinct on the timeline.

title: Add unit tests for ProfileService.getHistory(), ProfilesTable, AddMeasureModal, AddTreatmentModal, and profile form components
description: Several components and service methods have zero test coverage: ProfileService.getHistory() (public API with no unit tests), ProfilesTable.tsx, AddMeasureModal.tsx, AddTreatmentModal.tsx, ProfileList.tsx, ProfileEditor.tsx, ProfileHistory.tsx, and ProfileTimeline.tsx all lack Vitest tests despite handling critical clinical workflows.

title: Add HikariCP connection timeout, idle timeout, and leak detection configuration to all services
description: DatabaseFactory.kt initialises HikariCP without setting connectionTimeout, idleTimeout, or leakDetectionThreshold. A connection pool that never times out on acquisition will block request threads indefinitely under database load, and leaked connections (e.g. from unclosed transactions) will exhaust the pool silently.

title: Fix accessibility: form validation errors not linked via aria-describedby to their inputs
description: AddMeasureModal.tsx renders validation errors as role=alert divs but they are not associated with specific input fields via aria-describedby. Screen reader users hear the error message but cannot determine which field is invalid without re-navigating all inputs.

title: Convert /metrics endpoint from custom text format to Prometheus exposition format
description: kdiab-analyze's Metrics.kt returns metrics in a custom plain-text format (line 43) that is incompatible with standard Prometheus scrapers and Grafana. Switching to the Prometheus exposition format (using Micrometer or DropwizardMetrics-Prometheus bridge) would enable standard monitoring stack integration.

title: Fix glucose zone display: color-only encoding in MeasureList has no text fallback for color-blind users
description: MeasureList.tsx applies className 'glucose-low', 'glucose-target', 'glucose-high' to style readings visually by zone, but there is no accompanying text indicator ('(Low)', '(High)') in the element. Color-blind users cannot distinguish clinical glucose zones — a WCAG 1.4.1 violation.

title: Add health checks to Keycloak and kdiab-ui nginx containers in docker-compose
description: docker-compose.yml has no healthcheck directive on the Keycloak container (restart policy only) and no healthcheck on the kdiab-ui nginx container. Services that depend_on them cannot distinguish a healthy container from one that is starting or crashed, leading to authentication failures during platform startup.

title: Fix text-secondary color contrast: #94a3b8 on dark surface fails WCAG AA 4.5:1 minimum
description: CSS custom property --text-secondary is #94a3b8 on the dark --surface-color background, producing an estimated contrast ratio of ~4.2:1 for normal-weight text. WCAG AA requires 4.5:1 for normal text. Secondary text is used extensively for dates, labels, and supplementary information throughout the UI.

title: Fix inconsistent Instant types in BFF: AnalyticsService uses kotlinx.datetime.Instant, TimelineService uses java.time.Instant
description: The BFF has two incompatible Instant types in use side-by-side: AnalyticsService imports kotlinx.datetime.Instant while TimelineService imports java.time.Instant. This creates conversion overhead and risks subtle clock/timezone bugs where the two types interact at serialization boundaries.

title: Disable source maps in production Vite build
description: vite.config.ts enables sourcemap generation for production builds, exposing the original TypeScript source code, business logic, and API structure to anyone with browser DevTools. Source maps should only be generated for development or uploaded to an error tracking service, not served publicly.

title: Capture profile rejection reason when patient rejects a proposed profile
description: ProfileRoutes.kt rejectProposedProfile audits the rejection event but does not capture why the patient rejected it. Doctors have no way to understand whether the rejection was due to confusion, disagreement with the rationale, or a technical issue, losing valuable clinical context for follow-up.

title: Add patient notification trigger when doctor creates a PROPOSED profile
description: When a doctor creates a PROPOSED profile for a patient (ProfileRoutes.kt line 107-119), no notification mechanism exists — the patient only discovers the proposal on their next manual login. A notification (in-app badge, email, or push) is needed to ensure timely patient review of clinically important profile changes.

title: Display profile timezone field in ProfileEditor and ProfileList
description: The timezone field is persisted in the profiles database and returned by the API, but ProfileEditor does not show it as an input and ProfileList does not display it. Basal segment times are interpreted in the profile's timezone, so a clinician viewing a profile from a different timezone could misinterpret the schedule.

title: Fix unsafe Instant.parse() calls in mappers and services: wrap in BusinessValidationException
description: Instant.parse() is called without try/catch in MeasureMapper.toDomain(), TreatmentMapper.toDomain(), AnalyticsService (lines 66-67, 112-113), TimelineService (lines 23-24), and LocalTimeSerializer. Invalid ISO-8601 input causes uncaught DateTimeParseException that propagates as HTTP 500. These should be caught and rethrown as BusinessValidationException → 400.

title: Add pagination to profiles list endpoint (/users/{userId}/profiles returns unbounded array)
description: The kdiab-profiles list endpoint returns all profile versions as an unbounded array with no page/size parameters, while measures and treatments both have paginated list endpoints. A user with many profile versions (common with frequent adjustments) could cause OOM on both client and server.

title: Add pagination offset boundary tests for measures and treatments service layer
description: MeasureServiceTest and TreatmentServiceTest do not verify page offset edge cases: page offset beyond total count (should return empty list), page=0 with size=0, and very large page numbers. These boundaries are important because the frontend relies on empty-page detection to know when to stop fetching. The ExposedMeasureRepository and ExposedTreatmentRepository integration tests should also cover these cases.

title: Patient selector displays truncated UUIDs instead of human-readable names
description: The doctor's patient selector (in kdiab-ui) shows raw UUID strings truncated to fit the UI, making it difficult to identify patients at a glance. Doctors managing multiple patients (e.g. dr_house with both sarah and dr_cameron with mike) need a display name or at minimum the username from the JWT/Keycloak profile — not a UUID. This is both a UX problem and a patient safety concern (wrong patient selected).

title: Fix CLAUDE.md: backend tasks documented with :backend: prefix are incorrect
description: CLAUDE.md documents per-service backend commands as './gradlew :backend:run', './gradlew :backend:test' etc., but when running from within a service directory (e.g. kdiab-measures/) there is no ':backend' subproject — the tasks are directly on the root project. The correct commands are './gradlew run', './gradlew test', './gradlew check'. This misleads contributors into running wrong commands.

title: Add profile state machine transition tests for PROPOSED paths
description: ProfileStateMachineTest only covers DRAFT→ACTIVE and UPDATE transitions. PROPOSED→ACTIVE (patient accepts) and PROPOSED→ARCHIVED (patient rejects or doctor withdraws) state paths lack dedicated transition tests. Since the profile proposal flow is the primary doctor-patient collaboration mechanism, these transitions need explicit test coverage.

title: Add Vitest unit tests for TimeInRangeBar, TimelineChart, and AgpChart components
description: Three critical clinical data display components have zero Vitest unit tests: TimeInRangeBar (TIR zone colors and rounding), TimelineChart (Recharts ComposedChart with CGM/BGM/treatments), and AgpChart (5-layer AreaChart with percentile bands). These components are used for therapy adjustment decisions and need tests for zone color accuracy, data filtering, and tooltip content.

title: Add unit tests for AGP edge cases: single-bucket reading and negative glucose values
description: AnalyticsServiceTest has no test for AGP percentile calculation when a bucket has exactly one reading (all percentiles should equal that value) or when glucose data contains invalid negative values. These edge cases are clinically important — a single hourly reading could display misleading percentile ranges, and negative values indicate data corruption.

title: Add audit trail for measure and treatment deletion
description: Doctors and admins can delete patient measures and treatments but there is no frontend indication or backend audit record of who deleted what or when. Unlike profile changes (which have kdiab-profiles audit logs), deletion of measures and treatments leaves no trace. Add deletion events to the AuditLogsTable in kdiab-measures and an equivalent in kdiab-treatments.

title: Add createdBy field to profile proposals for doctor identification
description: Proposed profiles lack a createdBy/doctorId field, so patients cannot identify which clinician suggested the change or request clarification. The proposalReason was added (kdiab-8fr) but the authoring doctor's identity is still absent. This is a distinct concern from the reason text — patients need to know who to contact.

title: Wrap ExposedSQLException in domain exceptions in ProfileService
description: ProfileService catches raw org.jetbrains.exposed.v1.exceptions.ExposedSQLException directly in its create/update methods, leaking infrastructure exceptions through the application layer boundary. Infrastructure exceptions should be caught and wrapped in ConflictException or appropriate domain exceptions at the repository or service boundary to maintain hexagonal architecture.

title: Fix getTreatmentsByType: add date range filtering
description: TreatmentRoutes' getTreatmentsByType endpoint accepts a type filter but ExposedTreatmentRepository.findByUserIdAndType() has no from/to date filtering. title: Fix build.sh --clean: docker builder prune -af deletes build cache for pulled Docker Hub images
description:
## Problem

build.sh clean() runs:
  docker builder prune -af

This removes ALL build cache unconditionally, including cached layers for
pulled base images (postgres:15, nginx:alpine, quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:23.0,
dpage/pgadmin4:9.9.0). After --clean, the next docker compose up --build must
re-download all those layers from Docker Hub, even though --clean should only
reset locally-built kdiab artefacts.

Relevant code (build.sh lines 112-141):

  log "Removing local kdiab images"
  images=$(docker images --filter "reference=localhost/kdiab-*" -q ...)
  docker rmi $images ...

  log "Pruning Docker/Podman build cache"
  docker builder prune -af   ← removes everything, not just kdiab cache

## Expected behaviour

--clean should remove:
- Running containers (compose down -v)
- Locally built kdiab images (localhost/kdiab-*)
- Build cache entries belonging to kdiab images only

--clean should NOT remove:
- Pulled Docker Hub images (postgres, nginx, keycloak, pgadmin)
- Build cache entries for those Hub images

## Fix

Replace the aggressive docker builder prune -af with a targeted prune that
keeps cache entries still referenced by existing images. The --keep-storage
flag or filtering by label may help, but the simplest safe fix is to skip
builder prune entirely in --clean and optionally expose it as a separate
--purge flag:

  # Remove only dangling (unreferenced) build cache, not all cache
  docker builder prune -f 2>/dev/null || true   # dangling only, no -a

Or add a new --purge flag that runs the full prune for users who explicitly
want a complete reset including Hub image layers.
close_reason: Replaced prune -af with prune -f; dangling-only prune preserves pulled Docker Hub image layers

The measures and treatments list endpoints currently return all records for a user. Add optional `from` and `to` ISO-8601 timestamp query parameters for server-side date filtering. The BFF (kdiab-analyze) must also forward these params to the upstream services.

## Context

**Current state:**

# OpenSpec: Replace build.sh with root Gradle composite build tasks (kdiab-0my)

## Goal
`build.sh` is a 215-line Bash script that orchestrates Gradle builds for 4 backend services and an `npm ci && npm run build` for the `kdiab-ui` gateway frontend. The root `build.gradle.kts` already declares aggregate tasks (`build`, `check`, `clean`) that reference `:buildAll`, `:checkAll`, `:cleanAll` in each service — but those per-service tasks don't exist yet, so the aggregate tasks are broken. This issue implements the missing tasks, adds an npm Exec wrapper, and removes the Bash script entirely, giving developers a single `./gradlew` entry point for all monorepo builds.

## Context

**Root composite build:**
- `settings.gradle.kts` — includeBuild for all 4 services; no kdiab-ui (pure npm, no Gradle).
- `build.gradle.kts` — declares `build` (→ `:buildAll`), `check` (→ `:checkAll`), `clean` (→ `:cleanAll`) on each included build. These tasks currently fail because the per-service targets don't exist.

**build.sh — what it currently does:**
- Default: runs `./gradlew :build --no-daemon` in each service dir (in parallel via &) + npm build for kdiab-ui
- `--check`: same but `./gradlew :check`
- `--backend-only`: skip frontend
- `--frontend-only`: skip Gradle
- `--docker`: runs docker compose build for 8 images
- `--clean`: docker compose down -v + remove images + prune cache
- `--no-parallel`: sequential builds

**Per-service Gradle tasks (exist already):**
- `:build`, `:check` (= test + integrationTest + e2eTest + detekt + kover), `:clean`
- Each service build.gradle.kts is at the service root

**kdiab-ui:** pure npm/Vite project at `kdiab-ui/`. No build.gradle.kts. Not in composite build.

## Interface Changes
Command-line interface changes:

| Old (build.sh) | New (./gradlew) |
|---|---|
| `./build.sh` | `./gradlew build` |
| `./build.sh --check` | `./gradlew check` |
| `./build.sh --backend-only` | `./gradlew buildBackends` |
| `./build.sh --frontend-only` | `./gradlew buildFrontend` |
| `./build.sh --no-parallel` | `./gradlew build --no-parallel` |
| `./build.sh --docker` | `./gradlew dockerBuild` |
| `./build.sh --clean` | `./gradlew dockerClean` |

## Implementation Plan

**Step 1 — Add missing tasks to each service's build.gradle.kts (4 files)**

Append to each of kdiab-measures/build.gradle.kts, kdiab-profiles/build.gradle.kts, kdiab-treatments/build.gradle.kts, kdiab-analyze/build.gradle.kts:

```kotlin
tasks.register("buildAll") {
    group = "build"
    description = "Alias for 'build' — used by root composite aggregate task."
    dependsOn(tasks.named("build"))
}

tasks.register("checkAll") {
    group = "verification"
    description = "Alias for 'check' — used by root composite aggregate task."
    dependsOn(tasks.named("check"))
}

tasks.register("cleanAll") {
    group = "build"
    description = "Alias for 'clean' — used by root composite aggregate task."
    dependsOn(tasks.named("clean"))
}
```

**Step 2 — Update root build.gradle.kts**

Replace the current file with tasks: buildFrontend (Exec: npm ci + npm run build in kdiab-ui/), buildBackends (depends on :buildAll from all 4 services), build (depends on buildBackends + buildFrontend), check (depends on :checkAll from all 4 services), clean (depends on :cleanAll from all 4 services), dockerBuild (Exec: docker compose build), dockerClean (Exec: docker compose down -v + image removal).

**Step 3 — Delete build.sh**

`git rm build.sh`

**Step 4 — Update CLAUDE.md**

Replace the 'Full Monorepo Build' section commands with the new Gradle equivalents. Remove references to build.sh.

## Test Plan
- [ ] `./gradlew build` from repo root — compiles all 4 backends and builds kdiab-ui; BUILD SUCCESSFUL
- [ ] `./gradlew check` from repo root — all 4 service check tasks run; BUILD SUCCESSFUL
- [ ] `./gradlew buildBackends` — backends only; kdiab-ui npm NOT invoked
- [ ] `./gradlew buildFrontend` — npm ci + npm run build in kdiab-ui/; backends NOT invoked
- [ ] `./gradlew build --no-parallel` — sequential build; all services still succeed
- [ ] `./gradlew clean` — cleans all service build outputs
- [ ] `./gradlew tasks --all` — all new tasks visible

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `./gradlew build` succeeds end-to-end (4 backends + kdiab-ui)
- [ ] `./gradlew check` runs all unit + integration + e2e tests across all 4 services
- [ ] `build.sh` is deleted from the repository
- [ ] `CLAUDE.md` updated to document the new Gradle commands

## Risks & Assumptions
- Gradle parallel execution for included builds requires `--parallel` flag or `org.gradle.parallel=true` in gradle.properties. Test with `--info` to verify.
- The Exec tasks use `bash -c` — Linux-only, acceptable for this project.
- `dockerBuild` assumes `docker compose` (v2) — no podman fallback needed.
- Check each service build.gradle.kts for existing `buildAll` task before adding to avoid conflicts.

# OpenSpec: Refactor measures and treatments Liquibase changelogs to includes-based structure (kdiab-7xj)

## Goal
`kdiab-measures` and `kdiab-treatments` both define all changesets inline in a single `db.changelog-root.yaml` file. Extract the changesets into a `changes/001-ddl.yaml` file and replace the root file with an explicit `include` directive. Add `logicalFilePath` to the extracted file to prevent Liquibase checksum mismatches.

## Context

**Current state:**
- `kdiab-measures/src/main/resources/db/changelog/db.changelog-root.yaml` — flat file with inline changesets for the measures table.
- `kdiab-treatments/src/main/resources/db/changelog/db.changelog-root.yaml` — flat file with inline changesets for the treatments table (including a `dbms: postgresql` changeset for an index).
- `kdiab-profiles` already uses the includes pattern: `db.changelog-master.yaml` includes files from `changes/` — follow this exact pattern.

**Critical:** Liquibase identifies changesets by (filename, id, author) triple. Moving changesets to a new file changes the filename unless `logicalFilePath` is set.

## Interface Changes
No interface changes — Liquibase file reorganisation only.

## Implementation Plan

**kdiab-measures:**
1. Create `kdiab-measures/src/main/resources/db/changelog/changes/001-ddl.yaml` — copy all changesets from the current root file.
2. Add `logicalFilePath: db/changelog/db.changelog-root.yaml` at the top of `changes/001-ddl.yaml`.
3. Replace `db.changelog-root.yaml` with includes-only form pointing to `db/changelog/changes/001-ddl.yaml`.

**kdiab-treatments:**
4. Create `kdiab-treatments/src/main/resources/db/changelog/changes/001-ddl.yaml` — same extraction including the dbms:postgresql changeset.
5. Add `logicalFilePath: db/changelog/db.changelog-root.yaml` to `changes/001-ddl.yaml`.
6. Replace `db.changelog-root.yaml` with includes-only form.

## Test Plan
- [ ] `./gradlew :backend:check --no-daemon` in `kdiab-measures/` — integration tests (H2 + Liquibase) pass
- [ ] `./gradlew :backend:check --no-daemon` in `kdiab-treatments/` — same
- [ ] `docker compose up --build` from repo root — Liquibase init containers complete without errors

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Both services' Liquibase migration succeeds against a fresh DB
- [ ] Both services' Liquibase migration succeeds against an existing DB (no duplicate changeset errors)
- [ ] Quality gates pass; `logicalFilePath` present in both extracted files

## Risks & Assumptions
- `logicalFilePath` must match original file path in DATABASECHANGELOG table exactly: `db/changelog/db.changelog-root.yaml` (relative, no leading slash).
- The `dbms: postgresql` changeset in treatments is skipped by H2 — safe for integration tests.

# OpenSpec: Add upstream request latency logging to BFF HTTP clients (kdiab-8su)

## Goal
MeasuresClient, TreatmentsClient, and ProfilesClient log fetch start/end at debug level but record no timing. Operators cannot detect slow upstreams from logs. Wrap each httpClient.get() call with System.currentTimeMillis() timing and emit an INFO log with round-trip ms and HTTP status code. Log at WARN level on non-success responses.

## Context
All three clients are in kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/analyze/adapters/outbound/http/:
- MeasuresClient.kt: paginated loop; httpClient.get() at line 57 inside while loop; debug log at line 75
- TreatmentsClient.kt: single httpClient.get() at line 36; debug log at line 35
- ProfilesClient.kt: single httpClient.get() at line 30; debug log at line 29
- Logger: private val logger = KotlinLogging.logger {} in all three files

## Interface Changes
No interface changes.

## Implementation Plan

1. kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/.../adapters/outbound/http/TreatmentsClient.kt — Wrap the httpClient.get() call:
   val start = System.currentTimeMillis()
   val response = httpClient.get(...) { ... }
   val ms = System.currentTimeMillis() - start
   if (response.status.isSuccess()) {
       logger.info { "Fetched treatments from upstream in ${ms}ms [status=${response.status.value}]" }
   } else {
       logger.warn { "Upstream treatments returned ${response.status.value} in ${ms}ms" }
       throw UpstreamException(...)
   }
   Remove the existing pre-request debug log.

2. kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/.../adapters/outbound/http/ProfilesClient.kt — Same pattern around the httpClient.get() at line 30.

3. kdiab-analyze/src/main/kotlin/.../adapters/outbound/http/MeasuresClient.kt — Apply timing around each page request inside the loop. Track per-page timing and log per page. Also emit a summary log after the loop with total items, total pages, total elapsed time.

## Test Plan
- [ ] ./gradlew :check --no-daemon from kdiab-analyze/ — Detekt + Kover + existing tests green
- [ ] Manual: start the full stack, open Timeline tab — check logs for timing entries at INFO level

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Each upstream call logs round-trip ms at INFO level on success
- [ ] Non-success HTTP responses logged at WARN with status code and ms
- [ ] MeasuresClient logs per-page timing and a post-loop summary
- [ ] ./gradlew :check passes

## Risks & Assumptions
- System.currentTimeMillis() has ~1ms granularity — acceptable for HTTP latency logging.
- Existing debug logs that duplicate the new INFO logs should be removed to avoid log spam.

title: Add root Gradle project for monorepo builds
description: Replace build.sh with a proper Gradle composite build at the repo root so that a single './gradlew build' (or check/clean) drives all four services — backend Gradle + frontend npm — with parallel execution and IDE support.
design:
## Goal
Replace the proprietary build.sh with a root-level Gradle composite build that calls each service's backend (Gradle) and frontend (npm) builds through standard Gradle tasks.

## Context
- Four services: kdiab-measures, kdiab-profiles, kdiab-treatments, kdiab-bff
- All services already use Gradle 9.4.1 with their own settings.gradle.kts and version catalogs
- Each service's root build.gradle.kts currently only has the asciidoctor docs plugin
- No root-level Gradle project exists today
- build.sh handles parallel Gradle + npm builds via shell background processes

## Approach: Gradle Composite Builds
Each service stays an independent Gradle project (own settings.gradle.kts, version catalog, wrapper). Root uses includeBuild() to compose them. Services still build standalone via their own ./gradlew; root ./gradlew delegates to all four.

## Files to Create

### Root level (/home/triplem/projects/kdiab/)
- settings.gradle.kts — includeBuild for each of the four services
- build.gradle.kts — aggregate tasks: build, check, clean, buildDocker
- gradlew + gradle/wrapper/* — copied from any service (all use Gradle 9.4.1)
- gradle.properties — org.gradle.parallel=true, org.gradle.caching=true

### Root settings.gradle.kts
```kotlin
rootProject.name = "kdiab"
includeBuild("kdiab-measures")
includeBuild("kdiab-profiles")
includeBuild("kdiab-treatments")
includeBuild("kdiab-bff")
```

### Root build.gradle.kts
```kotlin
tasks.register("build") {
    dependsOn(
        gradle.includedBuild("kdiab-measures").task(":buildAll"),
        gradle.includedBuild("kdiab-profiles").task(":buildAll"),
        gradle.includedBuild("kdiab-treatments").task(":buildAll"),
        gradle.includedBuild("kdiab-bff").task(":buildAll"),
    )
}
tasks.register("check") {
    dependsOn(
        gradle.includedBuild("kdiab-measures").task(":checkAll"),
        ...
    )
}
tasks.register("clean") {
    dependsOn(
        gradle.includedBuild("kdiab-measures").task(":cleanAll"),
        ...
    )
}
```

## Files to Modify

### Each service's root build.gradle.kts (kdiab-*/build.gradle.kts)
Add frontend and aggregate tasks:
```kotlin
tasks.register<Exec>("buildFrontend") {
    workingDir = file("frontend")
    commandLine("bash", "-c", "npm ci --silent && npm run build")
    inputs.dir("frontend/src")
    inputs.file("frontend/package-lock.json")
    outputs.dir("frontend/dist")
}

tasks.register<Exec>("checkFrontend") {
    workingDir = file("frontend")
    commandLine("bash", "-c", "npm ci --silent && npm run lint && npm run test")
}

tasks.register("buildAll") {
    dependsOn(":backend:build", "buildFrontend")
}

tasks.register("checkAll") {
    dependsOn(":backend:check", "checkFrontend")
}

tasks.register("cleanAll") {
    dependsOn(":backend:clean")
    doLast {
        delete("frontend/dist")
    }
}
```

## Root Task Mapping
| ./gradlew command         | What runs                                    |
|---------------------------|----------------------------------------------|
| build                     | buildAll in all four services (parallel)     |
| check                     | checkAll in all four services                |
| clean                     | cleanAll in each service                     |

## What Stays in build.sh
The --clean Docker/volume teardown and --docker image build stay in build.sh. Alternatively buildDocker can be added as an exec task in root build.gradle.kts that calls 'docker compose build'.

## Acceptance Criteria
- ./gradlew build from repo root compiles all 4 backends and builds all 4 frontends
- ./gradlew check from repo root runs all tests, detekt, kover, and frontend lint/test for all services
- ./gradlew clean removes all build outputs
- Each service still builds independently via its own ./gradlew
- Parallel flag (./gradlew build --parallel) speeds up builds as build.sh --no-parallel does
- IDE (IntelliJ) can import the root project and see all four services as modules

## Risks
- npm wrapped in Exec tasks has no Gradle incremental support unless inputs/outputs are declared carefully
- Composite build task references (gradle.includedBuild().task()) cannot be used in dependsOn inside included builds themselves — only at root level
- If services diverge to different Gradle versions in future, root wrapper version needs updating
